title: Tracking where it goes
description: For one week, write down every spend — most people find one surprise.

body.heading: The one-week experiment
paragraphs: For seven days, note every purchase, however small: the snack, the app, the bus top-up. Use your phone notes or a scrap of paper. Do not judge as you go; just collect the facts.
At the end of the week, add it up by type. Small daily spends often total more than one big purchase, which is useful to know — you cannot adjust what you cannot see.

body.heading: Spot the patterns
paragraphs: Look for patterns rather than mistakes. Spending often clusters around tiredness, boredom, or routine — the same shop on the way home, the same delivery app on Friday night.

Pick just one pattern to experiment with. Maybe you bring a snack from home twice a week, or delete a saved card from a shopping app. One change, tested for a month, teaches you more than ten resolutions.

body.heading: Keep it light
paragraphs: Tracking forever can feel like homework. Many people track for a week every few months, like taking a photo of their habits, and that is enough to stay aware.

takeaway: Track every spend for one week, spot one pattern, and test one small change.
